claims.statement: For independent Y1,Y2,Y3 with densities <=1 and any symmetric invertible 3x3 B with sigma_min(B)=kappa, every affine quadratic Y^T B Y+2b^T Y+c has density norm <= (2*pi+3*sqrt(3))/kappa.

If an n-dimensional symmetric A has a principal coordinate 3x3 block with sigma_min >= kappa, then for independent coordinate densities <=1, ||p_{X^TAX}||_infinity <= (2*pi+3*sqrt(3))/kappa, with arbitrary couplings to all conditioned coordinates allowed.
If A has a positive- or negative-definite 2x2 principal coordinate block C, then ||p_{X^TAX}||_infinity <= pi/sqrt(det C), even with arbitrary cross-couplings to the conditioned coordinates.

For infinitely many n there are rank-three orthogonal projections A with three eigenvalues exactly 1 such that every 3x3 principal coordinate block has sigma_min <=3/n. Hence selecting one principal triple before conditioning necessarily loses dimension dependence on this family. Nevertheless sum_{|I|=3} det(A_II)=1 by Cauchy-Binet.

Convert the aggregate determinant resource carried by delocalized rank-three spectral directions (for a rank-three projector, sum det(A_II)=1) into a dimension-free density/small-ball bound without selecting one principal coordinate triple. A multilinear coarea/Brascamp-Lieb or equivalent product-measure inequality is the current exact bridge.

consumed_other_account_result.use: Accepted the source-backed correction that law-uniform pointwise Fresnel decay is false and used the completed diagonal C=pi branch as the baseline. The new theorem extends from diagonal forms to arbitrary nonsingular three-coordinate principal blocks and identifies the delocalized rank-three obstruction.
